title: Transform-and-Fix Scenarios Corpus and Eval Playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook describes a focused corpus and evaluation procedure for onboarding LLMs to Redwood’s code-generation and refactoring vertical. The goal is to produce repeatable, CI-friendly checks that measure: buildability (compilation), functional correctness (unit tests), preservation or improvement of style & readability, and regressions vs baseline models.

Scope and high-level approach
- Domain: small-to-medium sized Python and TypeScript microservices, algorithmic snippets, and test-driven refactors.
- Tasks covered: generate missing functions, refactor for testability, fix failing tests, reduce cyclomatic complexity, apply style constraints, and minimal breaking-change rewrites.
- Evaluation targets: models used in hosted and dedicated inference (quantized variants included).
- Prioritization: CI gating for onboarding (critical), nightly regression runs (important), exploratory manual evals (informational).

Corpus composition (design principles)
- Realistic variability: mix of single-file snippets and tiny multi-file packages (pkg < 200 LOC) that compile in isolation.
- Failure modes represented: off-by-one, wrong API usage, missing imports, async vs sync bugs, variable shadowing, and type errors.
- Refactor scenarios: extract function, rename with cross-file updates, split a long function into smaller units, add proper dependency injection for testability.
- Test-driven tasks: present a failing unit test and prompt the model to make the minimal code change to make the test pass.
- Style constraints: black/flake8 for Python, prettier/eslint for TypeScript; enforce single quote preference or project-specific rule subsets.

Scenario categories and examples
- Compile-Fix (CF): code that fails to compile/run. Prompt: "Make this module compile and pass 'make check' with minimal changes." Example: missing import and wrong return type.
- Test-Fix (TF): unit test failing; model asked to change code (not tests) to satisfy tests.
- Refactor-Split (RS): long function >50 lines; prompt asks to extract helpers and add unit tests.
- Style-Polish (SP): code that compiles and passes tests but violates style; prompt asks to refactor to meet style rules without changing semantics.
- API-Migrate (AM): small breaking change in dependency API; prompt requires minimal adapter to restore behavior.

Prompt templates (system/human style)
- System: "You are a senior engineer. Make minimal, well-documented changes. Preserve behavior unless tests require change. Include only code in the final answer unless asked for explanation."
- Human (Compile-Fix): "Project: <name>. Make the code compile. Run `python -m pytest` locally; change the implementation files only. Mark files you changed in the patch. Provide a unified diff."
- Human (Test-Fix): "A unit test in tests/test_x.py fails. Change implementation so all tests pass. Keep changes small and explain why you changed them in one short sentence. Return a git-style patch."

Scoring rubric (CI-friendly, automated)
- Buildability (40%): Does the repo compile / install / run basic linter? Binary pass/fail. For Python: pip install -e . + pytest exit code 0. For TypeScript: tsc/webpack build exit code 0.
- Functional correctness (40%): All provided unit tests pass. If additional tests are required by prompt (e.g., refactor asks to add test), those must pass too.
- Style & readability (10%): Lint score delta (lower is better). We normalize flake8/prettier errors per 100 LOC.
- Minimality (10%): Size of patch measured by lines changed (git diff). Smaller preferred; threshold set per scenario (e.g., <12 lines change preferred).

Automated harness expectations
- Input/Output format: model outputs must be a git-style unified diff wrapped in triple backticks or as a plain patch. If model gives prose, CI runner will flag as invalid.
- Execution runner: ephemeral container running the repo; apply patch, run install/build, then run tests and linters. Capture stdout/stderr and exit codes.
- Time budget: 60s per inference/sample for gating; nightly runs allow up to 300s.

Baseline results (example snapshot)
- Baseline model: redwood/codegen-x-small v1.2.0 (quantized variant used for nightly).
- Sample of 200 tasks (balanced across CF/TF/RS/SP/AM): compile pass 76%, all tests pass 68%, style improved 54%, median patch size 10 lines.
- Known cluster of failures: API-Migrate tasks with cross-file reference updates (drop to 40% correctness), async/await conversion mistakes in TypeScript.

Regression detection and thresholds
- Gate failure: any decrease >5 percentage points in 'all tests pass' on gating subset (n=40) compared to baseline triggers a hold.
- Nightly drift alert: >3 percentage points change for two consecutive nights opens AI-REG ticket automatically.

Failure analysis playbook (for SRE/Applied ML)
- Collect: failing sample inputs, model outputs (patch), test logs, linter output, container logs.
- Reproduce: re-run failing sample deterministically with same model seed & config.
- Triaging tags: "semantic-bug", "style-regression", "compilation-crash", "flaky-test-introduction".
- Common fixes: adjust decoding temperature, add stronger system instruction anchor, or prefer patch-size penalty during sampling.

Human review checklist (for onboarding PRs)
- Did the model change more than allowed LOC threshold? (Y/N)
- Do changes include new tests when requested? (Y/N)
- Any third-party API or dependency changes? (Y/N)
- Risk assessment: low/medium/high (note reason).

Known pitfalls and anti-patterns
- Overfitting to test suites: model writes brittle tests or disables assertions. Watch for test edits — policy: tests should not be modified unless prompt explicitly allows.
- Cosmetic-only outputs: pretty diffs that revert compile-critical changes. Ensure functional checks run.
- Multi-file rename ambiguity: models sometimes rename symbols without updating imports correctly -> fails compile.

Operational notes for CI integration
- Runner image: python:3.11-slim + node:18 LTS installed; caches for pip/npm.
- Sandbox: run as non-root, 30s network egress limit for package installs.
- Artifact retention: keep failing run logs + patches for 30 days; aggregate nightly metrics to Redshift.

Next steps (short-term)
- Expand corpus with 100 more API-Migrate and async-conversion tasks (owner: Ethan).
- Add mutation-based tests to stress variable naming and scoping (owner: Priya).
- Bake gating subset into PR checks for model-onboarding (target: Q2 2026).

Appendix: sample problem (Python Test-Fix)
- Prompt to model: "tests/test_math_ops.py shows one failing test. Change only code under math_ops/ to make all tests pass. Keep changes minimal. Return a git patch."
- Example expected model output: git unified diff touching math_ops/ops.py with a two-line fix and short commit message.

Contact
- Questions or sign-ups to help curate scenarios: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.example.com)
